Aisha: quick one — I'm prototyping a 'slice-based' quant compatibility approach so we can mix FP8 / INT8 / 4bit within a single model artifact. goal: runtime can pick per-slice precision based on prompt/latency/cost budget. pros/cons? :thinking:
Ben: sounds promising. main worry is metadata surface and backwards compat with older runtimes. how do you plan to encode the per-slice hints?
Aisha: idea is minimal header + optional calibration blobs. header fields: model_version, slice_table_offset, default_precision, compat_flags. then a slice table with entries like (slice_id, start_layer, end_layer, preferred_precision, calibration_checksum). small example:```
# pseudo header
model_version: 1
default_precision: fp8
slice_table_offset: 0x1f4
```
Carlos: calibration blobs will blow up artifact size. we have to choose between storing per-slice floats (calib stats) vs compact sketches. maybe store per-slice bias/scale int16 + seed for on-device quick recalib?
Eve: runtime contract question — should runtimes reject artifacts with unknown flags, or treat unknown flags as 'best-effort' and fall back to default_precision? mix of both would be safer: strict mode for Dedicated/Private, permissive for Hosted.
Aisha: agreed. propose two compatibility modes in header: strict=1 (reject on unknown), permissive=0 (best-effort). default to strict for enterprise tiers.
Ben: another operational concern: telemetry. we need per-request reporting of used precision per slice to attribute quality regressions. add a small telemetry version in header so we can evolve without breaking ingestion.
Carlos: fallback semantics: if a slice claims fp8 but runtime can't do fp8 fast on that hardware, fall back to next-best (int8 -> 4bit -> fp16). but we need a deterministic downgrade path encoded in header, otherwise behavior will diverge across runtimes.
Aisha: include downgrade_chain: [fp8, int8, 4bit, fp16] in slice metadata. runtime chooses first supported. sounds good?
Eve: testing matrix nightmare. recommend we require a tiny 'golden prompts' shard per model that we can run on upgrade to detect quality drops when migrations occur. store checksums + tolerances in header.
Aisha: yes — golden_prompts_checksum + per-slice deg_threshold. on dev flows, runtime can run quick eval for sanity before serving heavy traf.
Ben: implementability: loader will need to map slices -> kernels. we already have kernel registry keyed by (precision, kernel_variant). loader should validate all requested kernels present else fail early.
Carlos: runtime lockstep updates: when we add a new precision (eg fp8-e2), artifact should include a precision_alias table mapping alias->spec so old runtimes ignore unknown alias. supports forward-compat.
Aisha: good call. also thinking of 'quality escrow' field: a url to a hosted eval artifact (signed) where SRE/ML can re-run full checks if regression alerts fire.
Eve: security: calibration blobs may leak dataset stats. must encrypt blobs for Private deployments or mark them as 'redacted' and rely on on-device recalib. header should declare blob_encryption: none|kms|redacted.
DevBot: canary-deploy: quant-loader v0.9 pushed to staging at 2619876560 — watch for loader.failures metric.
Ben: ops note — add a lint step to model release pipeline that rejects artifacts with slice overlap or unsorted slice_table. common bug in early protos.
Aisha: agreed. final open q: should slice boundaries be layer-based or token-position-based? I vote layer-based for simplicity; token-position dynamic slicing is powerful but adds runtime complexity.
Carlos: layer-based + optional runtime remap for attention kv cache differences. that's flexible enough.
Eve: ok — I'll draft a short RFC with fields and a sample artifact layout. assigned to me, aiming EOD Friday. :rocket: 
Aisha: thanks all. follow-ups: Eve will post RFC, Ben will add loader validation checklist, Carlos will prototype compact calibration encoding, I'll wire up telemetry schema.
Ben: ack.
Carlos: ack, starting proto today.
Eve: posting RFC in #eng-ml later today.
DevBot: note: staging canary ended (2619876570) — no loader.failures observed. :white_check_mark:
